name: Worry and Unbelief

counsel.text: We are bid to "commit our way unto the Lord;" (Ps. 37. 5) the Hebrew word is, "roll thy way upon the Lord." It is our work to cast away care; (1 Pe 5. 7) and it is God's work to take care.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Art of Divine Contentment, ch. 1

counsel.text: By our immoderacy we take his work out of his hand. Care, when it is eccentric, either distrustful or distracting, is very dishonourable to God; it takes away his providence, as if he sat in heaven and minded not what became of things here below; like a man that makes a clock, and then leaves it to go for itself.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Art of Divine Contentment, ch. 1

counsel.text: God takes care of every saint in particular, as if he had none else to care for.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: A Body of Divinity, the providence of God

counsel.text: Let it be an antidote against immoderate fear, that nothing comes to pass but what is ordained by God's decree, and ordered by his providence. We sometimes fear what the issue of things will be, when men grow high in their actings; but let us not make things worse by our fear. Men are limited in their power, and cannot go one hair's breadth further than God's providence permits.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: A Body of Divinity, the providence of God

counsel.text: It is the property of faith to silence our doubtings, to scatter our fears, to still the heart when the passions are up. Faith works the heart to a sweet serene composure; it is not having food and raiment, but having faith, which will make us content. Faith chides down passion; when reason begins to sink, let faith swim.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Art of Divine Contentment, ch. 14

counsel.text: So will be thy relief from Christ. It will come in its season, as the dew and rain upon the parched ground; for faithful is he who hath promised.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

prayers.title: A prayer of confession
prayers.text: Father, I have not trusted you as I should. I have carried tomorrow in my own arms, as if you were not my Father and did not know what I need. My fears are not hidden from you, and you are gentle with them. But I confess the unbelief that would not rest in your care. Thank you that Jesus Christ the Righteous One speaks for me before you, and that his blood covers my doubting too. You know how I am made, and you remember that I am dust. Holy Spirit, put this distrust to death in me, and teach me to bring every care to you. I do trust you, Lord; help me where I do not. Amen.

prayers.title: When worry rushes in
prayers.text: Lord Jesus, my heart is racing and my thoughts run ahead to what might happen. You know what I need before I ask. I give you this care right now and leave it in your hands. You care for me more than I care for myself. Holy Spirit, quiet me, and turn my worry into prayer. Keep my mind fixed on you, and give me grace for this day only. I do trust you; help me where I do not. Amen.

prayers.title: When I am afraid
prayers.text: Father, I am afraid, and I thank you that I may tell you so. You feed the birds, and you have numbered the hairs of my head. Nothing can come to me today that you have not ordered in wisdom and love. I let go of what I cannot control and put it into your hands. Holy Spirit, fix my heart on Christ, who holds all things. Give me your peace, and strength to do the next right thing. Amen.

examinationQuestions: What were you anxious about today, and when the fear came, did you bring it to your Father or carry it alone?
Beneath the worry, what were you doubting about God: his power, his wisdom, or his love for you in Christ?
Which of God's promises did you forget today, and what would change if you believed it?
Are you trying to carry tomorrow's troubles with today's strength?
Has worry crowded out prayer, rest, or the Lord's Day, or kept you from serving others?
fleeActions: Tell God the worry out loud in one plain sentence, and leave it with him. Then turn to what you can do in the next hour.
Read Matthew 6:25-34 slowly, and ask your Father to help you trust him for today only.
Write down the thing you are afraid of, and beside it write one promise of God from his Word that answers it.
Ask a brother or sister in your church to pray for you today. Tell them plainly what you are afraid of.
Do the next ordinary duty in front of you, and do it as for the Lord. Leave tomorrow with him.
If this fear is heavy or keeps coming back, send your pastor a message today and ask to talk. Seeing a doctor as well is wise, not faithless.

afterFallReadings.text: Whether a Christian may not be sensible of his condition, and yet be contented? Yes; for else he is not a saint, but a stoic. Rachel did well to weep for her children, there was nature; but her fault was, she refused to be comforted, there was discontent.
afterFallReadings.author: Thomas Watson
afterFallReadings.source: The Art of Divine Contentment, ch. 5

afterFallReadings.text: Consider his mercifulness, tenderness, and kindness, as he is our great High Priest at the right hand of God. Assuredly he pities thee in thy distress; saith he, "As one whom his mother comforteth, so will I comfort you," Isa. 66:13. He hath the tenderness of a mother to a sucking child.
afterFallReadings.author: John Owen
afterFallReadings.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14
